title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Dispute Cases related to Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims

articles.content_en: Article 1: The provisions of the Special Maritime Procedure Law and the Maritime Law shall apply to the adjudication of cases involving disputes relating to limitation of liability for maritime claims; where the Special Maritime Procedure Law and the Maritime Law have no provisions, the provisions of other relevant laws and administrative regulations shall apply.

Article 2: Where, in the same maritime accident, different persons liable apply, before prosecution, to different maritime courts for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund pursuant to Article 102 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law, the maritime court that dockets the case later shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, transfer the case to the maritime court that docketed the case first for jurisdiction.

Article 3: Where a person liable applies in litigation for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund, the application shall be made to the maritime court that has accepted the relevant maritime dispute case.
Where the relevant maritime disputes are accepted by different maritime courts, and the person liable applies for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund, the application shall be made, pursuant to the litigation jurisdiction agreement, to the maritime court that first docketed the case; where the parties have not concluded a litigation jurisdiction agreement, the application shall be made to the maritime court that first docketed the case.

Article 4: After a maritime liability limitation fund has been established, the maritime court that established the fund shall have jurisdiction over actions brought by maritime claimants against the person liable in respect of disputes relating to the maritime accident.
Where a maritime claimant brings an action in another maritime court, the maritime court accepting the case shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, transfer the case to the maritime court that established the maritime liability limitation fund, unless the parties have concluded a litigation jurisdiction agreement.

Article 5: The period prescribed in the second paragraph of Article 106 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law, within which the maritime court shall make a ruling within fifteen days, shall be calculated from the thirtieth day counting from the day following the publication of the last announcement issued by the maritime court after accepting the application for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund.

Article 6: The date of expiry of the period for applying for registration of claims prescribed in Article 112 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law shall be the sixtieth day counting from the day following the publication of the last announcement issued by the maritime court after accepting the application for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund.

Article 7: Where a creditor applying for registration of a claim complies with the relevant provisions, the maritime court shall, after the establishment of the maritime liability limitation fund, make a ruling in accordance with the provisions of Article 114 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law; where the maritime liability limitation fund has not been established according to law, the maritime court shall rule to terminate the claim registration procedure. The application fees already paid by the creditor shall be borne by the person who applied for the establishment of the maritime liability limitation fund.

Article 8: After the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund, a maritime claimant may, on the basis of maritime compensation claims for which the person liable cannot invoke the defense of limitation of maritime liability according to law, apply for preservation of the property of the person liable.

Article 9: After the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund, where a maritime claimant applies for the arrest of a ship on the ground of exercising a maritime lien in respect of maritime compensation claims, arising from the same maritime accident, for which liability may be limited under Article 207 of the Maritime Law, the People's Court shall not support the application.

Article 10: Where a creditor, when instituting an action for confirmation of rights, asserts pursuant to Article 209 of the Maritime Law that the person liable is not entitled to limit liability, the assertion shall be made in writing. The trial of the case shall not apply the procedures for actions for confirmation of rights provided for in the Special Maritime Procedure Law, and the parties may, according to law, file an appeal against the judgment or ruling made by the maritime court.
Where two or more creditors assert that the person liable is not entitled to limit liability, the maritime court may consolidate the relevant cases for trial.

Article 11: After a creditor institutes an action for confirmation of rights pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 116 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law, where it is necessary to determine the proportions of fault of the colliding vessels, the trial of the case shall not apply the procedures for actions for confirmation of rights provided for in the Special Maritime Procedure Law, and the parties may, according to law, file an appeal against the judgment or ruling made by the maritime court.

Article 12: The ship operator specified in Article 204 of the Maritime Law means the registered ship operator, or a person who, upon the entrustment of the shipowner, actually uses and controls the ship and shall bear the liabilities of the ship, but does not include an operator of non-vessel-operating common carrier business.

Article 13: Where the person liable does not apply for the establishment of a maritime liability limitation fund, this shall not affect its raising, in litigation, of the defense of limitation of maritime liability against the maritime claims specified in Article 207 of the Maritime Law.

Article 14: Where the person liable does not raise the defense of limitation of maritime liability, the maritime court shall not, on its own initiative, apply the provisions of the Maritime Law concerning limitation of maritime liability in rendering its adjudication.

Article 15: Where the person liable does not raise the defense of limitation of maritime liability before the first-instance judgment is rendered, but raises it during the second instance or retrial, the People's Court shall not support it.

Article 16: Where the person liable does not raise the defense of limitation of maritime liability against the maritime compensation claims specified in Article 207 of the Maritime Law, and a creditor, on the basis of a relevant effective adjudication document or arbitral award, applies for enforcement against the property of the person liable other than the maritime liability limitation fund, the People's Court shall support the application, unless the creditor, using the above-mentioned documents as evidence of the claim, has applied for registration of the claim and has been permitted by a ruling of the maritime court.

Article 17: The maritime compensation claims for which liability may be limited under Article 207 of the Maritime Law do not include claims brought for the raising, removal, demolition or rendering harmless of a sunken, wrecked, stranded or abandoned ship, or claims brought for the removal, demolition or rendering harmless of cargo on board the ship.
Where, due to a collision of ships, the person liable is subjected to claims specified in the preceding paragraph, and the person liable seeks recourse against the other ship for the losses incurred as a result, and the respondent asserts that it is entitled to limit liability pursuant to Article 207 of the Maritime Law, the People's Court shall support the assertion.
Article 18: The 'person liable' specified in Article 209 of the Maritime Law refers to the person liable for the maritime accident himself.

Article 19: Where a maritime claimant asserts that the person liable is not entitled to limit liability on the ground that the ship involved in the maritime accident was unseaworthy, but cannot prove that the loss giving rise to the claim was caused by the intent of the person liable himself, or by his reckless act or omission with knowledge that such loss would probably result, the People's Court shall not support the assertion.

Article 20: A maritime liability limitation fund shall be established in Renminbi, and its amount shall be calculated in accordance with the method for converting Special Drawing Rights into Renminbi on the date when the court's ruling approving the establishment of the fund takes effect.

Article 21: The interest specified in Article 213 of the Maritime Law shall be calculated from the date of the occurrence of the maritime accident to the date of the establishment of the fund, at the loan prime rate for the same period published by the National Interbank Funding Center.
Where a maritime liability limitation fund is established by way of a guarantee, the interest during the period of establishment of the fund shall be calculated at the loan prime rate for the same period published by the National Interbank Funding Center.
Article 22: Where a People's Court conducts a retrial of a case that has been finally adjudicated before these Provisions come into force, these Provisions shall not apply.
Article 23: Where judicial interpretations issued by this Court before these Provisions come into force are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
